summary: Batch fan-out from cascading client retries creates long-tailed inference latency spike
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-12 08:40 UTC, TheraML is reporting sudden long-tail inference latency spikes (requests taking 10–60s) and client-side timeouts despite healthy model performance metrics on baseline traffic. Impact: customer-facing endpoints in their Dedicated pool (us-east) experienced degraded user throughput for ~45 minutes; some requests returned 504 client timeouts after multiple client retries.

Timeline and observed symptoms:
- 2026-03-12 08:40 UTC: First alert from TheraML (elevated tail latency).
- 08:42 UTC: Supporting metrics show a burst of 429s from internal soft-queue enforcement on the dedicated pool's rate-limiter.
- 08:43–09:25 UTC: Sustained increase in in-flight requests and CPU on nodes due to retries; autoscaler observed several short-lived scale-ups but capacity lagged.
- 09:30 UTC: Customer reports many client-side 504s and visible request replays from their SDK.

Environment: Dedicated GPU pool (dedicated), serving-runtime v2.12.1, api-gateway v1.9.3, region us-east, model variants listed above.

Steps to reproduce (customer repro path):
1) Simulate a burst of 50 concurrent user sessions each issuing sequential streaming generation requests with client SDK default retry (no jitter) and 4s connection timeout.
2) Observe initial 429 responses from our soft rate-limiter when sustained QPS exceeds configured burst window.
3) Clients retry immediately (no exponential backoff) which fans out requests across service and triggers internal request queueing, increasing tail latency.

Hypothesis: A combination of the customer SDK's aggressive, synchronized retry behavior and our soft 429 queueing (per-dedicated-pool burst window) caused an amplification loop. Retries inflated instantaneous concurrency, causing the serving runtime to enter a queued servicing state where requests are accepted but experience long queuing delays, which clients then interpreted as timeouts and retried again. Autoscaler reacted but with delay, and CPU/GPU contention amplified tails.

Observed logs and metrics referenced:
- Rate-limiter dashboards: elevated soft 429 count spike 08:41–09:10 UTC.
- Serving runtime telemetry: queue_depth 10x baseline, average K/V cache contention across shards.
- API gateway logs: multiple back-to-back POSTs from same client IPs with near-identical timestamps (evidence of synchronized retries).

Immediate mitigation taken: temporarily increased soft-queue threshold for TheraML's dedicated pool at 09:05 UTC and enabled per-connection jitter policy on the ingress proxy for their tenant to break synchronization. Recommended customer to deploy SDK patch with jittered exponential backoff.

Next steps: see investigation_notes and resolution entries below.

investigation_notes: Checked api-gateway logs: multiple identical POST retry sequences from same client SDK versions (no jitter), request spacing <200ms between retries.
Rate-limiter config: dedicated pool had burst_window_seconds=60 and burst_allowance=2500; soft-queueing triggers at 90% of allowance causing 429 soft responses instead of hard rejections.
Serving runtime: observed KV-cache lock contention and elevated GPU scheduling latency when queue_depth > 50; concurrent decode streams increased memory pressure.
Autoscaler behavior: scale-up initiated but min_replicas and cool-down settings delayed effective capacity increase by ~90s under this pattern.
Correlation: tail latency spikes correspond exactly to client retry storms; when synthetic clients introduced jittered backoff, tails normalized even without extra capacity.
resolution: Mitigation: 1) Temporary increase to soft-queue threshold for affected tenant on 2026-03-12 09:05 UTC to reduce 429s. 2) Enabled per-tenant ingress jitter for duplicate connections to desynchronize retries. 3) Customer deployed SDK patch (jittered exponential backoff) and confirmed reduced errors. Follow-ups: created INT ticket to tune autoscaler cooldown and add per-tenant spike alerts; engineering RFC to harden serving-runtime queueing semantics and add early-shed behavior when queue depth exceeds safe threshold.
postmortem_actions: Create INT ticket to reduce autoscaler cooldown for dedicated pools handling low-latency customers (owner: infra/autoscaler).
Add per-tenant hard-shed policy when queue_depth > 75% to avoid long-tailed queuing (owner: serving-runtime).
Ship guidance in the DevDocs + SDK release notes recommending jittered exponential backoff and recommended client retry windows for streaming endpoints.
Instrument a dashboard showing per-tenant retry amplification signal and an alert to SRE when correlation exceeds 0.6.
